In case G is a matrix Lie group, the exponential map reduces to the matrix exponential. The exponential map, denoted exp:g → G, is analytic and has as such a derivative ⁠d/dt⁠exp(X(t)):Tg → TG, where X(t) is a C1 path in the Lie algebra, and a closely related differential dexp:Tg → TG.\nThe formula for dexp was first proved by Friedrich Schur (1891).","description":"Formula in Lie group theory","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}
